POTENTIAL ANZACS. Young Australian schoolboys in their teens are required to complete a course of military training every year. A campis held annually and the citizen forces are trained for three weeks under service conditions. The picture shows the raw material, of fine physique, being issued with uniforms and kit from the store in Melbourne Victoria. Australia will be well represented at the next war too.

ARRIVAL OF BRITISH SERVICE SQUADRON. On the afternoon of the arrival of the British Service SQuadron, officers and men of the various ships to the number of 1500 marched through Sydney Streets. This photo shows portion of the procession and gives an idea of the crowd which thickly lined the route.

PINCHGUT - was the name the soldiers in olden days gave this small fort situated on a rocky islet at the head of Sydney Harbor. It is properly known as Fort Denison. Its old fashioned guns date back to Waterloo. One is still used to signal the time each day and is here seen firing. Fort Denison will be gaily decorated for the Duke's arrival.

ARMISTICE DAY. Armistice Day Commencoration was impressively depend in Sydney on November 10 by a route march of trainees and returned soldiers, and all arms were represented in the parade. The picture shows the Seventh Field Artillery, with their 18-pounder guns, passing out of the Domain near the Mitchell Library, where Sir William Cullen, the Lieutenant-Governor, took the salute.

COMMONWEALTH LOAN RALLY: When this crowd had gathered in Martin Place, Sydney, to watch a steeplejack paint the flagstaff of the Commonwealth Bank, nearly 200 feet above the street, the bank authorities threw from the parapet, thousands of envelopes containing theatre tickets, first instalments on the new conversion loan, and propaganda. There was a wild scramble in the street, and the loan received a considerable impetus.
BUILT IN A DAY

Bridge building efforts of some raw engineers at Moore Park, Sydney, their first camp. There were about 200 First Divisional Engineers in the camp. Some of them came from North Sydney, some from Newcastle.

Allies D y, Nov. 19th, was celebrated with a lot of enthusiasm at Sydney, Nov. South Wales, Australia. The booths represent the different nations that are fighting for the Allies. Articles of all kinds were sold from the mk booths, the funds going towards swelling the Allies' D y Collection.

ANZAC DAY IN MELBOURNE. An impressive march of returned soldiers was made through Melbourne on Anzac Day 25th April). The processor is shown turning from Swanston Street into Bourke Street Melbourne.
ANZAC DAY IN SYDNEY. - ROSEMARY FOR REMEMBRANCE. In the City Streets on Anzac Day, April 25, soldiers as well as civilians were wearing rosemary.

held in Melbourne by Dock workers.

OUTSIDE THE PREMIER'S OFFICE. The picture shows some of the unemployed men who made an undisciplined raid on the Government offices at Melbourne Victoria in the hope of securing orders for meals and beds from the Premier Mr. Allan.
STOLEN GOODS
Sale

Transactions, good, bad, and informant Court yesterday, when fully 500 people surrounded the auctioneer, who had goods scheduled as unclaimed and stolen, explained that all purchases would be for cash, and that none of the goods carried guarantees. The majority of the 420 lots disposed of in parcels of 48 bottles. Being the proceeds of raids on sly grip shops, there is a possibility of much of the liquor being that some of it had a very suspicious appearance. The average price of these lots was in the neighborhood of 24%. Wine was there in plenty, lots of 24 bottles changing hands for 33.

A feature of the proceedings was the knowledge that some of the dealers evicted as to the contents of many sealed cases of miscellaneous goods. The prices paid for these lots varied considerably, as good as the other. There was a deal of team-working too. One man was noticed following the auctioneer from lot to lot and occasionally emitted a peculiar whistle. The sound was the signal to a mate, who, on hearing it, would commence to bid freely.

TO MEET OLD FRIENDS: Scene at Central Railway Station, Sydney, on the arrival of Lord Allenby, the conqueror of Palestine, who at the signing of the Armistice commanded the territory from Constantinople to Uganda in Africa.

THE SOLDIERS FRIDEN. Almost every Australian and New Zealand soldiers who passed through Durbin researchers Kiss Campbell, who, as every troopship neard the port, stood on the brinkwater and somephored greetings, and information concerning the whereabouts of the various organisations which catered for the soldiers' welfare. And she was the last to be then farewell. Kiss Campbell, with her father and mother, is visiting Sydney. She was given a wonderful welcome by returned soldiers, and was entertained by the State Government at Parliament House, Photo shows Kiss Campbell with the original flags.
MR. Holloway, Secretary of the Victorian Trades Hall Council, seen leaving Melbourne (Victoria) by the "Moldavia" to represent Australia at the International Labor Conference at Geneva.

AUSTRALIAN VINES are improving in quality every year. Shown in this picture are some of the judges sampling the vines entered for the annual competition.

FOR CAR SOUTH SEAS. A party of ten runs and three priests have just arrived in Sydney from France on their way to the islands of the Pacific where they will undertake the hazardous task of ministering to the lepers exiles on Makogai Island, Fiji. Photo shows two of the priests arriving in Sydney.
WHAT WOULD YOU DO? This is how Sydney collects money for her hospitals. Scenes like this occur at regular intervals throughout the year.

A unique feature of the Progress Association'sx Carnival held at Portsea ( a popular Victorian seaside resort ) was a historical pageant depicting Portsea's discovery by Captain Cook. The picture shows "Captain Cook" planting the British flag.
Some of the huge crowd of 110,000 people at Flemington Racecourse. Melbourne, for the Melbourne Cup.
STUDYING IS WORTH WHILE. 60 Melbourne University graduates think so, when photographed after their degrees had been conferred upon them by General Sir John Monash.

THE GOVERNOR GENERAL'S GARDEN PARTY. The beautiful grounds of Federal Government House, Melbourne, were thronged with uniformed men and beautifully dressed women at Lord and Lady Forster's party. Picture shows guests assembled in the fountain court after tea.

THE ANNIVERSARY COMMEMORATION of the introduction of the eight hours working day is held annually in Victoria on May 5th. The symbol, 8.8.8 represents eight working hours and roughly eight hours recreation, and eight hours sleep. Over three hundred ex-policemen, dismissed for striking in the recent police strike in Melbourne, marched and are seen in the photograph turning from Bourke into Spring Street, Melbourne.

DIGGERS ORGANISE TO FIND EMPLOYMENT. A meeting at the Diggers' Unemployment Bureau in St. Mary's Church Hall, Fitzroy, Melbourne. A list has been prepared showing the type of work each man is capable of doing, and it is hoped jobs will be found for all of them within a month, In the meantime, assistance is given where possible to needy cases. On the board in front are pinned offers of employment that have been received. On the left is the Anglian commissioner, Rev, C.C. Barclay, who is treasurer of the Bureau.
FOREST OF BANNERS: International Scout service at Sydney Town Hall attended by Lord and Lady Stonehaven and Sir Dudley and Lady de Chair. Scoutss from all over the world were present.

CENTURY OF LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL: This photograph was taken at the special meeting of the Legislative Council of New South Wales on August 25, to celebrate the centenary of responsible Government in this State. The first advisory council was appointed on August 25, 1824.

Dawn of Australia's history - It was on this rock at Kurnell Botany Bay, 153 years ago that Captain Cook made his first landing in Australia. Last week there was an impressive celebration on the shore close to this spot. The Governor-General, Lord Forster, delivered a stirring speech.

ST KILDA'S WAR MEMORIAL, was unveiled at St Kilda (Victoria) on Anzac Day. The picture shows the crowd which attended the ceremony.

Death for a wash--- The well at the head of the Anzae " Valley of death" formerly one of the most dangerous places in the whole zone. A good drink and a wash always rewarded those who risked their lives in reaching the well.
ANZAG DAY IN SYDNEY: Many sad scenes were witnessed at the memorial opposite the gates through which the New South Wales soldiers all passed on to the wharf to embark on the transports.

GREAT FOOTBALL SEASON: The present Sydney football season promises to be one of the best on record. The visit of the English Rugby team has given the game a fillip. Photo shows portion of the crowd of 55000 which watched the first match between Queensland and New South Wales teams.
TO WELCOME THE FLEET: A few of the Defence Department's D.H9 bombers which flew out to sea and escorted the American Fleet to Sydney Harbor.
PLANE LIKE A BAT... WORKED BY FOOT FROM BICYCLE SADDLE SEAT.
AT INVENTOR'S AMBITION.

It seems that the age of the Bird Man is rapidly approaching if the expectations of a young inventor, Mr. H.S. Dixon, late of the Australian Air Force, come true. Mr. Dixon, who is 34, has for many years, dreamt of the day when men shall strap wings to their backs and fly, like the birds at will, and he believes that within a year or two he will be able to make this possible. Out of the Unemployment dole he has managed to buy materials for the construction of a 30ft. self-propelled aeroplane which in appearance is exactly like a gigantic bat. The curved planes which are manipulated by foot pedals move up and down like a bird's wing and the seat is an old bicycle saddle. Pressure on the pedals depresses the planes after atmospheric pressure has elevated them and the weight of the passenger is distributed by means of an ingenious arrangement of elastic springs.
Photo shows.... Mr. H.S. Dixon with his invention.

SYDNEY-ADLAIDE AERIAL MAIL: The aerial mail between Sydney (NSW) and Adelaide (South Australia) has passed the experimental stages and has maintained a regular service through all kinds of weather for the past three months. Photo shows the mail being put aboard at Sydney for delivery in Adelaide the following day. The distance between the two cities is about 700 miles.

AERIAL DERBY IN AUSTRALIA. AERIAL DERBY IN AUSTRALIA is holding its first Aerial Pageant at Richmond (N.S.W.) among low-powered, Australia is holding its first Aerial Pageant at Richmond (N.S.W.) among low-powered, and judging from the keen aeroplanes, constructed for the most part in the Commonwealth, and judging from the keen enthusiasm of the pilots, mechanics and everyone else concerned, it should prove the enthusiasm of great aerial carnivals with machines wholly built in Australia. This week forerunner of great aerial carnivals with machines wholly built in Australia. This week has been devoted to reliability tests and next Saturday (December 6th) all the machines has been devoted to reliability tests and next Saturday (December 6th) all the Australian will compete in the Aerial Derby. Photo shows Squad-on-Leader Wackett in the all-Australian plane in which he made a sensational landing after a preliminary demonstration. His plane plane in which he made a sensational landing after a preliminary demonstration, it taxied along the ground was travelling at a speed of 60 miles an hour when it landed, it taxied along the ground was travelling at a speed of 60 miles an hour, and it seemed certain of crashing into a police barrier without any mishap.

AERIAL CARNIVAL AT MICHMOND (NEW SOUTH WALES). This little Broadsmith biplane was designed by Captain Broadsmith, owned by Mr.Delacarthur Onslow, and entered by "The Sun" for all the events in the Aerial Derby, held at Richmond on p December 6, piloted by Captain E.W. Percival it won the light-powered competition for Australian-built aeroplanes with points to spare, breaking an American record, taking first place in four out of seven separate tests, thus earning the Lobbeus Hordern £500 prize for the best all-round machine.

THRILLS AT RICHMOND. N.S.W. The last week in May was full of thrills for the Flying Officers of the Richmond Flying School, and it was agreed that the first parachute descents in Australia from speeding planes were eminently successful. Flying Officer V.Augenson, a young graduate from Dumtroon (MSW) was the first member of the Richmond aerodrome class to descend. Photo shows him "trying gut" the parachute.

AERIAL CARNIVAL AT RICHMOND (NEW SOUTH WALES) The principal event of the carnival - the Aerial Derby - had to be postponed on account of bad weather, until December 8. The race was won by Capt.F.W.Follett in the Defence Department's D.H.37 machine, but as the departmental 'planes were non-competitive the prize went to Lt.H.C.Miller, a Queensland competitor who was flying an Ascet Avro. It.Miller carried off both prizes in the Aerial Derby as he recorded the best speed performance among non-departmental machines as well as winning the Handicap.

AERIAL DERBY. On November 29th 1924 an aerial pageout is to be held at Richmond aerodrome (New South Wales) for one week, and the competitions among low-powered aeroplanes, constructed for the most part in Australia represent a distinct step towards what this country must eventually do. Every encouragement is being offered to thoseyoung Australians engaged on the machines, and next week's trials should prove the forerunner of future great aerial pageants with machines wholly built in the Commonwealth. Photo shows one of the two baby 'planes of the Department of Civil Aviation entered for the Aerial Derby.

Mr. Dixon, who is 34 has for many years dream of the day when men shall strap wings to their backs and fly, like the birds, at will and he believes that within a year or two he will be able to make this possible. Outof the unemployment dealer he has managed to buy materials for the construction of a 30ft. self-propelled aeroplane. In appearance the machine is exactly like a gigantic bat. The curved places which are manipulated by foot pedals move up and down like a bird's landing and the seat is an old bicycle saddle. Pressure on the pedals depresses the plans after atmospheric pressure has elevated them end arrangement of elastic springs.

TO FLY ROUND AUSTRALIA. The Fairy D.3. Aeroplane in which Wing-Commander S.J.Goble, and Flying Officer I.E.McIntyre have started on a flight round Australia for Naval Reconnaissance purposes. They left Sydney Melbourne on April 6 and flew to Sydney through a heavy rain and wind storm. From Sydney they flew to Southport, Queensland.
PASSION FOR THE AIR: Lord and Lady Stonehaven photographed after leaving the Aerial mail plane which flies from Adelaide to Cootamundra (NSW).

IN AN ENCLOSED SEMI-CIRCLE the weather and travelled stained seaplane that carried Wing-Commande's Goble, and Flight-Lieut. MacIntyre round the coastline of Australia, reposed in safety. As the day wore on the crowd of its advisers grew alarmingly, until the police had to keep a sharp lookout for souvenir hunters.

TRIPLE OF OPAL: This remarkable example of the gem-cutters art can be held in the hollow of the hand. The little temple is entirely constructed of fire opal and black opal, and presents a wonderful appearance. It is the work of a Sydney man.

Leaving Government House. The Governor General of Australia, Lord Forster, leaving Government House, Melbourne to open the Australian Parliament on Wednesday, June 13th. Beside him rides a guard of lancers.
HONORSING SCOTCH POET: Every year Scotsmen gather about the statue of Bobbie Burns in the Domain, Sydney, and do honor to his memory. Photo shows this year's ceremony.

BOBBIES BIRTHDAY.

On January 25, a crowd of Sydney Scots, with full pipe bands, gathered at the Status of Robert Burns in the Sydney Domain to do honor to the poet on the 184th anniversary of his birthday.
AUSTRALIA BUILDS CARS. Some of the motor cars which are now being built by General Motors in Sydney, New South Wales.

HIS PASSPORT. - A row of fine service medals, Capt. Munsha Singh of the Indian Army who fought at Gallipoli, France, in Iraq and Afghanistan, has come to Australia. He wants to settle in New Zealand if the Government will let him. He thinks he has earned the right to make a living in a white man's country that once belonged to the Maoris.

GRAND OPERA BABY'S FATHER Signor Amleto Tornari the Prompter in the opera at His Majesty's Theatre Melbourne (Victoria) has just become the proud father of a daughter. Dame Nellie Melba is to be the child's godmother. Signor Tornari was a busy but happy man.

VICE ROYALTY AT FOOTBALL. The Governor of Victoria Lord Stradbroke accompanied the South Melbourne V. St. Kilda match played at the South Melbourne Football Ground. The photograph shows left to right: Hon. George Rous Mr. Cuthbertson, President of South Melbourne Club, and Lord Stradbroke.
NEW PRESIDENT FARMERS & YSETTLERS
Mr. H.B.Thorby, M.L.A., the President of the Farmers & Settlers Association which has just concluded its annual Conference in Sydney.

"LOOKING US OVER". Viscount Elmley, (eldest son and heir of the 7th Earl Beauchamp who was Governor of New South Wales from 1899 to 1901), who has been spending some weeks in getting bush experience in this country. He is very favourably impressed with conditions offered to settlers in Australia, and promises to boost Australia on his return to England and to induce the right kind of settlers to immigrate to Australia. Photo shows Viscount Elmley on board the S.S.Houtman outward-bound for Java.

WALSH AND JOHNSON APPEAL TO HIGH COURT. Sir Robert Parran, Solicitor-General of the Commonwealth (on the left) and Mr.Lamb K.C., (on the right) who acted for the Commonwealth Government in the High Court Case against Tom Walsh and Jacob Johnson. The latter are trying to secure their release from Garden Island (Sydney) where they are being detained until the settlement of the Departation case.

ENGLISH RUGBY LEAGUE TEAM: The English Rugby League Team which arrived in Sydney on May 28, and which will attempt to wrest "the ashes" from Australia, was given a civic reception at the Sydney Town Hall. Photo shows the Premier of New South Wales (Sir George Fuller) welcoming Mr J.Harry Dannatt, manager of the team.

OPENING OF REY SOUTH WALES PARLIAMENT: Although a Labor Government is in power, Parliament was opened on August 18 with all the usual pump and ceremony. This picture shows the scene in the Legislative Council. The Governor is in the chair in the centre of the dais. On his right is Mr Fred Flowers, President of the Legislative Council, and on his left is General Brand, state Commandant.

FEDERAL CABINET MEETS AT CANBERRA. The firstmeeting of the Federal Cabinet to be held at Canberra (New South Wales) Australia's Federal Capital in the making, took place on January 30,1924, at Yarraalumla Homestead, near the site of the future capitol. Photo shows the Cabinet meeting. On the left side Senator Crawford (Hon.Min) Mr Bowden (Min for Defence) Mr Austin Chapman (Min for Cubms) Sir Lyittleton Groom (Attorney General). At the head of the table Dr Earle Page (Acting Prime Minister). On the right side, left to right Mr Atkinson (Hon.Min) Mr Gibson (P.M.G.) Mr Stewart (Works & Railways) and Senator Pearce (Home & Territories).
